searches.answer: The sources indicate that Generative AI is a significant trend in cloud computing, with hyperscalers like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud competing on the power and integration of their GenAI platforms. AWS Trainium2 instances and Azure's enhancements in the Azure OpenAI Service are highlighted as part of these trends. Additionally, quantum computing in the cloud is noted as a developing area, with all three major hyperscalers offering "Quantum-as-a-Service" platforms. The sources also mention the growth of cloud spending and the strategic shift towards multicloud interconnects, with AWS and Azure leading in this space.

searches.answer: Kubernetes 1.20 will begin to deprecate Docker runtime support, with plans to remove it entirely in version 1.22. This change is due to Docker runtime's non-compliance with the Container Runtime Interface (CRI) for Kubernetes. Users of open-source Kubernetes clusters will need to make changes to avoid disruptions. Docker Desktop release notes indicate updates to Kubernetes, Docker Engine, and other components, but do not specifically mention Docker runtime deprecation. Kubernetes documentation confirms the removal of dockershim and advises on migration from it.

results.title: Container Runtimes | Kubernetes
results.content:
#### Note:

Kubernetes releases before v1.24 included a direct integration with Docker Engine, using a component named dockershim. That special direct integration is no longer part of Kubernetes (this removal was announced as part of the v1.20 release). You can read Check whether Dockershim removal affects you to understand how this removal might affect you. To learn about migrating from using dockershim, see Migrating from dockershim.
